prerequisites: Successful completion of the design modules of a Bachelor's degree.
Basic knowledge of "Methodical Product Development" or "Agile Methods of Product Development" are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can classify the essential sub-areas of product development and their underlying scientific approaches within the general subject context.
Students can explain the methods of product development and their properties and application possibilities regarding their classification in relation to Industry 4.0.
Students can critically evaluate requirements for product development based on their current methodological expertise, demand appropriate additions, and create a plan for suitable method deployment.
Students can develop products from the requirements list to the finished product, considering the technical complexity of the chosen method.
Students develop products using innovative methods, tools, and processes related to Industry 4.0 by applying their didactic and methodical repertoire in a target group-oriented and diverse manner.
Students can present their work results orally and in writing in a clearly structured form.
Students can adequately assess the result of their product development with respect to the specified requirement profile.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of product development and Industry 4.0
Innovative and classic methods in the product development process
Advanced approaches for function-oriented, cost-effective, and manufacturing-friendly product design
Digital Engineering and interface to production and other processes
assessment_rules: A accompanying term paper is to be prepared. This can be done as an individual task or in a small group, with the scope of work adjusted accordingly. As part of the term paper, the result of a small, self-contained product development will be documented and presented. The developed product must have been created at least as a "virtual prototype" using suitable methods and CAE systems available in the laboratory. Regular attendance is required as an ungraded examination.
